```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 0.3)

# draws n full-width blank lines (margin to margin) for handwritten answers,
# as a single plot so spacing is deterministic; pair with fig.height = 0.3 * n
blank_lines <- function(n = 1) {
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, n), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    segments(0, n - i + 0.5, 1, n - i + 0.5, lwd = 1)
  }
}

# keeps a prompt and its answer space on one PDF page: place `r nq(...)` on its
# own line just above the prompt. Emits nothing in non-LaTeX output. lines =
# lines of prompt text, rows = rows of blank space below it (0.3 in each),
# extra = any other height (in inches), e.g. a code block
nq <- function(lines, rows = 0, extra = 0) {
  if (!knitr::is_latex_output()) return("")
  knitr::asis_output(sprintf("\n\\needspace{%.2fin}\n", 0.23 * lines + 0.15 + 0.3 * rows + extra))
}
```

```{r key-helpers, include=FALSE}
ans_col <- rgb(200, 0, 130, maxColorValue = 255)
# redraws blank_table() so cells flagged TRUE in `ans` use the answer color
blank_table <- function(headers, body, col_widths = NULL,
                        header_height = 0.35, row_height = 0.5,
                        cex = 0.95, bold_rows = integer(0), ans = NULL) {
  nc <- length(headers); nr <- length(body)
  if (is.null(col_widths)) col_widths <- rep(1, nc)
  col_widths <- col_widths / sum(col_widths)
  cx <- c(0, cumsum(col_widths))
  h_total <- header_height + nr * row_height
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0), family = "serif")
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, h_total), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "",
       xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i")
  y <- h_total
  segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = 1.5)
  y <- y - header_height
  segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = 1.5)
  for (i in seq_len(nr)) {
    y <- y - row_height
    segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = if (i == nr) 1.5 else 0.5,
             col = if (i == nr) "black" else "grey70")
  }
  for (v in cx) segments(v, 0, v, h_total, lwd = 1)
  yh <- h_total - header_height / 2
  for (j in seq_len(nc)) text((cx[j] + cx[j + 1]) / 2, yh, labels = headers[[j]], font = 2, cex = cex)
  y <- h_total - header_height
  for (i in seq_len(nr)) {
    yc <- y - row_height / 2
    for (j in seq_len(nc)) {
      val <- body[[i]][[j]]
      is_ans <- !is.null(ans) && isTRUE(ans[[i]][[j]])
      if (!identical(val, "")) text((cx[j] + cx[j + 1]) / 2, yc, labels = val, cex = cex,
                                    font = if (i %in% bold_rows) 2 else 1,
                                    col = if (is_ans) ans_col else "black")
    }
    y <- y - row_height
  }
}
```

```{r key-values, include=FALSE, cache=TRUE}
options(cmdstanr_no_ver_check = TRUE)
library(cmdstanr)
myxo <- read.csv("../../data/MyxoTiter_sum.csv")
titer <- myxo$titer[myxo$grade == 1]
myxo_code <- "
data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  vector<lower=0>[N] titer;
}
parameters {
  real<lower=0> shape;
  real<lower=0> scale;
}
model {
  titer ~ gamma(shape, 1 / scale);
}
"
myxo_model <- cmdstan_model(write_stan_file(myxo_code))
dat <- list(N = length(titer), titer = titer)
fit <- myxo_model$sample(data = dat, chains = 4, parallel_chains = 4, seed = 746,
                         refresh = 0, show_messages = FALSE)
summ_full <- fit$summary("shape")
n_div <- sum(fit$diagnostic_summary()$num_divergent)
ci_full <- quantile(fit$draws("shape", format = "draws_matrix"), c(0.025, 0.975))
fit_short <- myxo_model$sample(data = dat, chains = 4, parallel_chains = 4, seed = 746,
                               iter_warmup = 20, iter_sampling = 50,
                               refresh = 0, show_messages = FALSE)
summ_short <- fit_short$summary("shape")
f2 <- function(v) formatC(v, format = "f", digits = 2)
```

\ans{\textbf{Answer key.} Answers are in magenta. Stan results vary a little from computer to computer.}

## Part 1: Install Stan

We'll use **cmdstanr**, the R interface to Stan. The full instructions
are at <https://mc-stan.org/cmdstanr/articles/cmdstanr.html>; the short
version:

1. **Get a C++ toolchain.** Windows: install Rtools for your version of
   R (<https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/>). Mac: in the
   Terminal, run `xcode-select --install`.
2. **Install the package and Stan itself**, in R:

```{r install-code, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("cmdstanr",
                 repos = c("https://stan-dev.r-universe.dev", getOption("repos")))
library(cmdstanr)
check_cmdstan_toolchain(fix = TRUE)   # checks (and tries to fix) the C++ setup
install_cmdstan(cores = 2)            # downloads and builds Stan; be patient
cmdstan_version()
```


**1a.** What does `cmdstan_version()` report?
If the installation failed, write the error message you got stuck on.

CmdStan version: \ans{2.39.0 or newer (any recent version is fine)}

\ans{(Only if it failed.) Common culprits: Rtools missing or the wrong version (Windows), command line tools not installed (Mac), or a path with spaces or non-English characters.}

## Part 2: Fit Wednesday's myxo model

Here is the model from Wednesday's lecture (myxomatosis virus titers,
Gamma distribution, flat priors on the positive values). Copy it into
an R script and run it. Stan compiles the model to C++ the first time,
which takes up to a minute.

```{r myxo-code, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
library(cmdstanr)
myxo <- read.csv(
  "https://kevintshoemaker.github.io/NRES-746/data/MyxoTiter_sum.csv")
titer <- myxo$titer[myxo$grade == 1]

myxo_code <- "
data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  vector<lower=0>[N] titer;
}
parameters {
  real<lower=0> shape;
  real<lower=0> scale;
}
model {
  titer ~ gamma(shape, 1 / scale);  // Stan's gamma uses shape and rate
}
"
myxo_model <- cmdstan_model(write_stan_file(myxo_code))
fit <- myxo_model$sample(data = list(N = length(titer), titer = titer),
                         chains = 4, parallel_chains = 4, seed = 746)
fit$summary()
fit$diagnostic_summary()
```


**2a.** Record these from the output (yours may differ a little from a
classmate's):

$\hat R$ for shape: \ans{`r f2(summ_full$rhat[1])`} \qquad effective sample size (`ess_bulk`) for shape: \ans{about `r round(summ_full$ess_bulk[1])`}

Number of divergent transitions (all chains): \ans{`r n_div`}

95% credible interval for shape (hint: `quantile()` on
`fit$draws("shape", format = "draws_matrix")`): \ans{about `r round(ci_full[1])`} to \ans{`r round(ci_full[2])`}


**2b.** *(Recommended: no AI.)* Now make the sampler work much less
hard: rerun the `sample()` call with `iter_warmup = 20` and
`iter_sampling = 50` added. How do $\hat R$ and the effective sample
size change, and why would you not trust these results?

$\hat R$ for shape: \ans{`r f2(summ_short$rhat[1])` (example run; well above 1.01)} \qquad `ess_bulk` for shape: \ans{about `r round(summ_short$ess_bulk[1])` (example run)}

\ans{R-hat rises well above 1.01 and the effective sample size collapses: 20 warmup draws aren't enough for NUTS to tune its step size, and the four chains haven't converged to the same distribution. Summaries from these draws would be unreliable.}
